src/user/dto/login-user.dto.ts: LoginUserDto { @IsNotEmpty() email, password }: a request payload for login

Graph: index.ts re-exports all three DTOs, and user.controller.ts and user.service.ts import all three, which shows they are used as one unit
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files have a single job: they define the request DTOs for the user feature (create, login, update). Each is a plain readonly data class, and the same three classes are consumed together by user.controller.ts and user.service.ts through index.ts. None of them contains logic, unrelated concerns or calls that go around another abstraction in the module. CreateUserDto and LoginUserDto both mark email and password with @IsNotEmpty. That repetition is the usual way to declare per-request validation in DTOs, not a copied business invariant. UpdateUserDto has no class-validator decorators. That fits a partial-update payload, but its fields are not marked optional (no ? and no @IsOptional), so the update contract is less explicit than the others. This is a minor stylistic gap, not a split concern or a bypassed abstraction, so the unit passes.
